question_text: Oscar decides to start a new business venture which involves taking out a bank loan. The bank charges an interest rate of $6.55\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly. His quarterly repayments are $\$933.62$, and must be repaid over 8 years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Entering TVM parameters with $N = 32, I\% = 6.55, \text{PMT} = -933.62, FV = 0, P/Y = 4, C/Y = 4$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The borrowed amount is the present value $PV$ of an annuity given quarterly payments, interest rate, and term.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Setting $P/Y$ or $C/Y$ to 12 instead of 4 for quarterly payments.

subparts.stem: How much interest will he pay over the 8 year period?

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating total repayments minus principal borrowed

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Total interest paid over the life of a loan is given by $\text{Total Repayments} - \text{Principal Borrowed}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using simple interest formula instead of subtracting principal from total repayments.

subparts.stem: Calculate the outstanding balance at the end of the sixth year.

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting $N = 24$ in TVM solver to find balance after 6 years

subparts.solution:
$N = 6 \times 4 = 24$, $I\% = 6.55$, $PV = 23\,110.12$, $\text{PMT} = -933.62$, $P/Y = 4$, $C/Y = 4$
$\therefore FV \approx -6947.33$
So, the outstanding balance is $\$6947.33$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The balance of the loan at any time is the future value $FV$ after the specified number of periods.
step_by_step: Solve for $FV \approx -6947.33$, so the outstanding balance is $\$6947.33$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Calculating $N$ using remaining quarters (8) rather than elapsed quarters (24).

subparts.stem: At the end of the 6th year, Oscar pays a lump-sum of $\$3000$ off the loan. Assuming his repayments remain the same, how much sooner will Oscar repay the loan?
subparts.solution:
$I\% = 6.55$, $PV = 6947.33 - 3000 = 3947.33$, $\text{PMT} = -933.62$, $FV = 0$, $P/Y = 4$, $C/Y = 4$
$\therefore N \approx 4.417$
It will take another 5 quarters to pay off the rest of the loan.
$\therefore \text{time saved} = 8 \times 4 - (6 \times 4 + 5) = 32 - 29 = 3$ quarters

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A lump-sum payment directly reduces the outstanding principal balance. The remaining time is calculated using the new reduced balance as $PV$.
step_by_step: Solve for $N$ using TVM solver with $\text{PMT} = -933.62$ and $FV = 0$, obtaining $N \approx 4.417$.
Round up to 5 quarters for complete payoff.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding $N = 4.417$ down to 4 instead of rounding up to 5.
